work.problem: The inference instance template runs as ci-runner-vm, which can read the runner GitHub App key (Playbook issue #103). Journal and register it (severity high, owner-confirmed 2026-11-17) and add SEC-014; the fix lands in sovereign-vpc-gcp under the same ticket.

findings.reason: Same root: a workload or agent acting with an identity meant for something else. This fix narrows the runner identity's blast radius; F-0046 is the agent side. The commits keep the clone's configured author (Claude), never one set on the command line (F-0096).
Its lesson applies to this branch: no user.name/user.email on the command line; the configured identity authors every commit.
Branch protection on sovereign-vpc-gcp is unchanged by this work; the fix PR still merges only through the owner's review.

#38 moved only the GPU bench's account into the human-applied identity unit, and the main inference unit was left on the runner's account; F-0097 records that applies failed with 'iam.serviceAccounts.create denied' for exactly this reason. The correction reuses #38's pattern (the account in the identity unit, ci-apply may attach it).
findings.revalidation: Re-read on main at 35e8ba3: modules/identity/main.tf lines 158-179 still define ollama-gpu-bench with logWriter and metricWriter and apply_uses_inference_bench; live/dev/gcp/inference/terragrunt.hcl line 39 still passes runner_sa_email. The pattern applies unchanged.

findings.reason: Apply is broken and disabled (F-0085), so the unit change cannot roll a new template until apply runs again. The identity unit is applied by the owner by hand, as for #38.
apply.yml is disabled_manually: the corrected template reaches GCP only after apply is re-enabled. Verification must read the live template list, not the merged code.
No platform behaviour is assumed from memory: the check reads the plan JSON fields the existing no-delete gate already reads (resource_changes[].change.after), and its fixtures are plan JSON.
The guardrail counts only with a designed-to-fail case: a fixture plan whose instance template uses ci-runner-vm must fail, and the runners unit and a dedicated account must pass.
findings.revalidation: tests/gates/*/cases.sh in sovereign-vpc-gcp still run from gates-selftest.yml on pull requests that touch tests/gates/**; the new cases follow the auto-merge cases' shape.

findings.reason: A check merged without running is the failure F-0092 records. The check script runs in the self-test on its own PR, before it is wired into plan.
The check verifies its input explicitly (the plan JSON parses and has resource_changes) and fails closed, not relying on set -e inside a condition.

Diagnose from live state, not declared code: the finding's evidence is the owner's instance-templates list, and KAN-30's Nov 3 comment confirms a VM actually ran as ci-runner-vm. The register entry says so instead of 'latent' only.
Runner scaling and queued-job alerts are not touched.
The runner image is not touched.
The gates' Python path is not touched; the check is bash and jq on hosted runners.

lessons: Move the account into the human-applied identity unit first, then point the unit at it in a second change (#38's pattern, KAN-30's order), so no plan reads a missing output (#39).
Ship the guardrail with a designed-to-fail fixture and run it before wiring it into plan (F-0010, F-0092).
Record what live state showed: a VM ran as ci-runner-vm from 2026-10-23, confirmed 2026-11-03 (KAN-30), so the exposure was not only latent (F-0086).
A known finding sat 14 days on a ticket with no journal entry or register row, so production readiness never counted it.
uncertainty: Whether the key was read while a VM held the runner identity cannot be shown: secret read logging was off (KAN-30, 2026-11-05). The runner App key was rotated on 2026-11-16 and the old version disabled.
The plan-time check sees only units planned in CI; a template created by hand outside Terraform is caught only by the live verification.
